topic: What antenna design considerations balance inter-beam interference reduction with flexible coverage adaptation in precoding-enabled satellites?
consensus_response: To balance inter-beam interference reduction with flexible coverage adaptation in precoding-enabled satellites, consider the physical mechanism of array factor shaping. The number of beams (n_b) impacts frequency bandwidth allocation (BW_FD), as evident from Table I. For n_b = 10, BW_FD = 250 MHz [Source: construction-of-a-flexibility-analysis-model-for-flexible-high-throughput-satellite-communication-systems-with-a-digital-channelizer_tables_tables.json, P.7]. Increasing N reduces mainlobe width but increases sidelobe level, affecting inter-beam interference reduction and flexible coverage adaptation. This tradeoff has budget implications in terms of reduced spectral efficiency due to increased IBI. Adaptive Coding and Modulation (ACM) can be used to adapt transmission parameters based on channel conditions, further reducing IBI while ensuring efficient use of spectral resources.
